papers.title: The Neurochemical Basis of High-Altitude Sleep Disruption: Disentangling Respiratory and Sleep-Circuit Mechanisms Toward Targeted Pharmacotherapy.
papers.summary: Reviews the neurochemical basis of high-altitude sleep disruption, using a randomized controlled trial where acetazolamide reduced AHI and improved oxygenation but did not restore N3 slow-wave sleep or sleep efficiency. Proposes a dual-target framework involving serotonergic, adenosinergic, orexin/hypocretin, and locus coeruleus norepinephrine nodes plus HIF-1α.

papers.title: A Computational Model Captures Orexin-Dependent Modulation of Memory Consolidation.
papers.summary: A rate-based computational model links orexinergic tone-dependent sharp-wave ripple statistics to memory performance, combining an encoding module with an OX2R-driven consolidation module. The model predicts task-dependent effects: encoding-dominant learning benefits from increasing orexin drive, whereas consolidation-dominant learning is non-monotonic with an internal optimum, and effective consolidation depends on task complexity reflected in sequence length.

papers.title: Revisiting post-stimulus theta activity: evidence for a broadband rather than narrowband spectral origin.
papers.journal: The Journal of neuroscience : the official journal of the Society for Neuroscience
papers.summary: Using high-density EEG in children across audiovisual and visual oddball tasks, this study tested whether post-stimulus theta increases reflect narrowband oscillations or stimulus-driven aperiodic changes. After explicitly modeling and removing aperiodic activity, the apparent theta increase was largely abolished and beta desynchronization was overestimated by conventional methods, while alpha desynchronization remained robust.

papers.title: When Charon Knocks at the Sleep Laboratory: Are European Heatwaves an Underrecognized Methodological Challenge for Sleep Research?
Exploratory analysis of electroencephalogram activity preceding nocturnal enuresis episodes using home-based sleep monitoring.
papers.summary: In 18 children with primary nocturnal enuresis, home-based single-channel EEG showed higher delta-band power at 10 and 5 minutes before enuresis onset on wet nights versus the same clock times on dry nights, with total power also elevated at 5 minutes. The findings suggest transient sleep deepening precedes enuresis, but no differences appeared at 30 minutes before onset.

papers.title: Evolved differences in microglial cell biology between surface and cave populations of Astyanax mexicanus.
papers.summary: This study developed an experimental toolbox to examine microglial specification, dynamics, and function in Astyanax mexicanus and compared surface and cave morphotypes. Cave populations showed increased microglial numbers over development, lower lysosomal pH, expanded proteolytic compartments, and a rapid inflammatory expansion distinct from zebrafish.

papers.title: What drives intersubject correlation of EEG during auditory narratives?
papers.summary: Using temporal response functions and correlated component analysis on EEG from participants listening to auditory narratives under passive, attentive, and distracted conditions, the study assessed contributions of acoustic and linguistic features to intersubject correlation. Acoustic features explained more variance and were the main ISC contributors, attention-related ISC increases involved all features, and word surprisal affected ISC only during active engagement, with a small overall portion explained by linear TRF responses.

papers.title: Effects of Gallic Acid on Sleep and Circadian Rhythm in a Drosophila melanogaster Model of Fragile X Syndrome: An Integrative Behavioral and Bioinformatic Approach for Target Predictions.
papers.journal: The Yale journal of biology and medicine
papers.summary: Assessed gallic acid effects on sleep and circadian rhythm in a Drosophila model of fragile X syndrome across seven concentrations using video monitoring. Gallic acid altered sleep and circadian parameters in a concentration-dependent manner, most pronounced at lower concentrations, with bioinformatic predictions implicating Rac1, bsk, Jra, Cyfip, and Dscam1.

papers.title: An evidence-weighted knowledge framework with path-aware reasoning for personalized lifestyle management in chronic disease.
papers.summary: The paper constructed an Evidence-Weighted Lifestyle Knowledge Graph (EW-LKG) from over 170,000 PubMed abstracts, comprising 156k entities and 202k relations, to support personalized lifestyle management in chronic disease. Path-aware question answering improved accuracy across four large language models, with gains up to 0.184, and correct answers were associated with higher PathScores (0.80 vs. 0.62).

papers.title: Links of fitbit-derived sleep architecture and fragmentation with ADHD symptoms and externalizing behaviors in adolescents.
papers.summary: In 4,545 ABCD Study adolescents, lower absolute and proportional REM sleep was associated with higher ADHD symptoms but not externalizing behaviors after multiple-testing correction, whereas greater wake after sleep onset was associated with higher ADHD symptoms and less robustly with externalizing behaviors. Light and deep sleep were not significantly associated with either outcome.

papers.title: Distinct brain network organization in asynchronous and synchronous motor observation and motor imagery: evidence from EEG functional connectivity, phase-amplitude coupling, and decoding.
papers.summary: The study investigated whether asynchronous and synchronous motor observation and motor imagery (MOMI) exhibit distinct EEG network patterns during a basketball set-shot task. Results showed condition-related differences in theta, alpha, and beta functional connectivity, stronger theta-gamma phase-amplitude coupling in asynchronous MOMI, and a decoding accuracy of 69.61%, with asynchronous MOMI achieving the highest classification accuracy (79.41%).

papers.title: Longitudinal associations of rapid eye movement (REM) sleep and slow-wave sleep with plasma Alzheimer's disease biomarkers.
papers.journal: Alzheimer's & dementia : the journal of the Alzheimer's Association
papers.summary: Longitudinally examined associations of REM sleep and slow-wave sleep with plasma Alzheimer's disease biomarkers in 64 cognitively unimpaired older adults over 2.6 years. Frontal slow-wave activity was cross-sectionally associated with plasma Aβ42/40, whereas low REM sleep percentage predicted faster annualized decline in Aβ42/40, especially in amyloid-positive participants.

papers.title: Weight Management in Obesity-Associated Sleep-Disordered Breathing: Mechanisms, Clinical Management, and Emerging Therapies.
papers.journal: Endocrine practice : official journal of the American College of Endocrinology and the American Association of Clinical Endocrinologists
papers.summary: This narrative review summarizes mechanistic links between obesity and sleep-disordered breathing and practical management approaches, including positive airway pressure and weight-directed therapies. It reports that tirzepatide has shown clinically meaningful reductions in apnea-hypopnea index in adults with obesity and moderate to severe obstructive sleep apnea, largely associated with weight reduction.

papers.title: Recent and Cumulative Cannabis Use and Sleep in Middle-Aged Adults.
papers.summary: This cohort study analyzed 35-year data from the CARDIA study to examine associations of cumulative and recent cannabis use with objective and subjective sleep in middle-aged adults. Each additional cannabis-year was associated with higher odds of low sleep percentage (OR 1.10), high sleep fragmentation (OR 1.04), and prolonged WASO (OR 1.21); recent use was also associated with poorer objective sleep, but no association was found with subjective sleep quality.

papers.title: Feasibility and Methodological Consideration of Using Wearable Devices to Examine the Relationship Between Sleep and Balance: Case Report With 2 College Students.
papers.summary: This case report assessed the feasibility of using consumer-grade wearable devices for longitudinal sleep tracking and explored descriptive visual trends between sleep patterns and balance performance in two college students over four months. Missing data rates were initially high but improved with structured weekly check-ins; wearables showed excellent within-participant agreement for total sleep time (ICC=0.97-0.99) but poor agreement for specific sleep stages, and exploratory trends linked sleep timing fluctuations to balance scores.

papers.title: Rest-activity rhythms, sleep dimensions, and mortality in adults with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome: A survey-weighted NHANES cohort study.
papers.summary: In a survey-weighted NHANES cohort of 3061 adults with cardiovascular-kidney-metabolic syndrome, higher rest-activity rhythm fragmentation (intradaily variability) was associated with increased all-cause mortality (HR 1.15 per 0.1 unit), while higher relative amplitude was associated with lower mortality (HR 0.74 per 0.1 unit); longer mean sleep duration and higher sleep efficiency were also associated with lower mortality, and greater sleep-midpoint variability with higher mortality.

papers.title: Effect of Computer Screen Background Hues on Attention, Memory, and Visual Task Performance in Medical Students: A Repeated Measures Pilot Study.
papers.summary: In a repeated-measures pilot study with 30 medical students, short-duration cognitive task performance differed significantly across computer screen background hues (balanced white, red-predominant, blue-predominant) and printed white paper, with printed paper showing the highest mean correct-response percentages on several tasks (e.g., 89.92% vs. 71.40% for white screen) and red-predominant screen performing better than balanced white on selected attention and recall outcomes.

papers.title: LTPat-based SOXFE: A self-organized explainable feature engineering model for automated fibromyalgia detection.
papers.journal: Technology and health care : official journal of the European Society for Engineering and Medicine
papers.summary: The study evaluated a self-organized explainable feature engineering (SOXFE) model for EEG-based fibromyalgia classification using sleep EEG data, achieving record-wise leave-one-record-out (LORO) accuracy of 92.77% for NREM stage 2 and 97.00% for stage 3, with complementary segment-level 10-fold cross-validation reaching 100% accuracy; the authors caution that participant linkage was unavailable and subject-wise validation is needed.

papers.title: Which cognitive emotion-regulation strategies are implicated in the association between sleep quality and negative affect?
papers.summary: This preregistered cross-sectional study examined cognitive emotion regulation as a mediator between sleep quality and negative affect in 899 adults. Poorer sleep quality was associated with greater negative affect, with indirect effects through maladaptive regulation strategies such as self-blame, rumination, and catastrophizing.

papers.title: Obstructive sleep apnoea and Alzheimer's disease pathology: a review of plausible pathological mechanisms and potential modifying impact of hypertension.
papers.summary: This review synthesizes existing literature on plausible pathological mechanisms linking obstructive sleep apnoea (OSA) to Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology, including oxidative stress and altered sleep architecture, and discusses the potential modifying impact of comorbid hypertension on AD pathogenesis, highlighting the need for research on the combined effects of OSA and hypertension.

papers.title: Hemoglobin Exhibits a U-Shaped Association with Obstructive Sleep Apnea at High Altitude: Machine-Learning and Exploratory Interventional Evidence.
papers.summary: In 250 men residing at high altitude, hemoglobin (Hb) exhibited a U-shaped association with obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) severity, with the lowest apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) in the 170-210 g/L Hb group (P < 0.001); a machine-learning model for OSA classification achieved an AUC of 0.873, and in an exploratory substudy, erythrocytapheresis was associated with larger short-term reductions in Hb and AHI and improved nocturnal oxygenation compared with oxygen therapy alone.

papers.title: Acute partial sleep deprivation attenuates cardiac output during moderate-intensity cycling in young adults.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Heart and circulatory physiology
papers.summary: In a randomized crossover trial of 25 young adults, acute partial sleep deprivation (40% of normal sleep duration) attenuated cardiac output at 60 minutes of moderate-intensity cycling and during recovery, with lower estimated ejection fraction and higher total peripheral resistance. The reduced cardiac output was attributed to a blunted stroke volume without compensatory heart rate increase.

papers.title: Rev-erb-α in Skeletal Muscle Adaptation: Integrating Circadian Control Mechanisms and Exercise Dynamic Responses.
papers.summary: This review consolidates experimental evidence on the role of Rev-erb-α in skeletal muscle adaptation to exercise, highlighting its circadian regulation and pleiotropic actions. It reports that exercise induces bimodal Rev-erb-α regulation, with downregulation immediately post-exercise followed by an increase, and that higher physical activity increases its 24-hour amplitude.

papers.title: Night-shift work is associated with peripheral clock gene dysregulation and circadian transcriptional network remodeling in female healthcare workers.
papers.summary: This study experimentally validated a circadian gene panel and investigated YY1 in 93 female healthcare workers, finding that night-shift workers showed significantly lower expression of CLOCK, TEF, PER1, and YY1 compared to day-shift workers. A four-gene model discriminated groups with AUC 0.940, improved to 0.976 with YY1.

papers.title: Longer sleep duration and the incidence and progression of diabetic nephropathy: a prospective cohort study.
papers.summary: In 678 Japanese outpatients with type 2 diabetes, mean sleep duration was the only lifestyle factor associated with a composite endpoint of incidence and progression of diabetic nephropathy. Compared with <6 hours, the multivariable-adjusted hazard ratios for 7 to <8 and ≥8 hours were 1.56 (95% CI, 1.05-2.31) and 1.92 (95% CI, 1.15-3.19), respectively (P for trend = .003), indicating that longer, but not shorter, sleep duration is associated with increased risk.

papers.title: Complementing Engel Classification: Postoperative Scalp EEG as an Objective Indicator in SEEG-Guided Radiofrequency Thermocoagulation-A Seizure-Onset Pattern-Based Stratified Analysis.
papers.journal: Annals of clinical and translational neurology
papers.summary: In a retrospective cohort of 25 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy undergoing SEEG-guided radiofrequency thermocoagulation, low-voltage fast activity (LVFA)-present seizure-onset patterns were associated with higher seizure freedom (92.3% vs 33.3%, p = 0.004) and postoperative scalp EEG normalization (87.5% vs 33.3%, p = 0.028) compared with LVFA-absent patterns. Postoperative EEG normalization may serve as an objective complement to Engel classification.

papers.title: Abnormal sleep duration and sarcopenia are jointly associated with adverse depressive trajectories in adults aged ≥45: Evidence from a longitudinal cohort study.
papers.summary: Using data from 11,295 and 6,739 participants in the China Health and Retirement Longitudinal Study, this study found that abnormal sleep duration combined with sarcopenia was associated with increased odds of first-onset depressive symptoms and adverse depressive trajectories. Specifically, the combined group had higher odds of belonging to the rapidly elevating depressive trajectory (OR=4.130, 95%CI: 2.455-6.948) and the slowly elevating trajectory (OR=2.436, 95%CI: 1.700-3.941) compared with the reference trajectory.

papers.title: Prevalence of adult attention-deficit/ hyperactivity disorder symptoms among university students and their relation to sleeping duration, time management skills, and academic performance.
papers.summary: This cross-sectional study estimated the prevalence of adult ADHD symptoms among 612 university students in Saudi Arabia and examined associations with sleep duration, time management, and academic performance. It found a 26% prevalence of ADHD symptoms, with significant associations with female sex (OR=1.58), sleeping fewer than 4 hours per night (OR=2.46), and lower GPA (OR=2.10).

papers.title: A Qualitative Exploration of Barriers and Facilitators to Changing Provider's Current Evaluation and Treatment Decision-Making for Velopharyngeal Insufficiency.
papers.journal: The Cleft palate-craniofacial journal : official publication of the American Cleft Palate-Craniofacial Association
papers.summary: This qualitative study interviewed 28 surgeons and 16 speech-language pathologists from 12 cleft teams to identify barriers and facilitators to changing evaluation and treatment decision-making for velopharyngeal insufficiency. Providers required evidence of improved speech outcomes or reduced obstructive sleep apnea risk, and favored applying new approaches to complex cases or defined subgroups rather than broad adoption.

papers.title: Maternal Circadian Preference is Associated With Cardiorespiratory Fitness and Participation in Structured Prenatal Exercise.
papers.summary: In pregnant women from two randomized controlled exercise trials, greater evening chronotype was associated with lower cardiorespiratory fitness (VO2peak) and significantly lower compliance with a structured prenatal exercise program. Exploratory analyses found a significant Time × Chronotype interaction for HDL cholesterol, which increased from 16 to 36 weeks' gestation in morning-oriented women but did not change in evening-oriented women.

papers.title: Advantage of cerebellar intermittent theta-burst stimulation in Alzheimer's disease (ACT-AD): study protocol for a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial.
papers.summary: This protocol describes a multicenter, randomized, double-blind, sham-controlled trial (ACT-AD) that will evaluate the efficacy and safety of long-term, neuronavigated cerebellar intermittent theta burst stimulation (iTBS) in 100 patients with mild-to-moderate Alzheimer's disease. The primary outcome is change in the Clinical Dementia Rating Scale Sum of Boxes score from baseline to week 12.

papers.title: National trends in chronic kidney disease prevalence by sleep duration in South Korea, 2007 to 2022: A nationwide cross-sectional study.
papers.summary: Analyzing 87,246 Korean adults from the Korea National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (2007-2022), this study found a U-shaped association between sleep duration and chronic kidney disease prevalence. Compared with 7-8 hours, fully adjusted odds ratios for CKD were 2.34 (95% CI, 2.04-2.69) for <6 hours and 2.07 (95% CI, 1.77-2.41) for ≥9 hours, with the pattern persisting after adjustment for cardiometabolic comorbidity and perceived stress.

papers.title: Hyperactive Delirium Temporally Associated With Hydroxyzine in a Child With Succinic Semialdehyde Dehydrogenase Deficiency Presenting With Psychotic Symptoms: A Case Report.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 12-year-old girl with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase deficiency (SSADHD) who presented with psychotic symptoms and developed hyperactive delirium temporally associated with hydroxyzine exposure, which was discontinued. Low-dose quetiapine and environmental interventions led to improvement in sleep, appetite, and behavioral regulation.

papers.title: Environmental noise pollution and its association with temporomandibular joint disorders, malocclusion, and bruxism: A Comparative cross-sectional study of adults in high-traffic and low- traffic areas.
papers.summary: In a comparative cross-sectional study of 300 adults in New Delhi, high-traffic residents had significantly higher prevalence of temporomandibular disorders (61.3% vs 25.3%), bruxism (42.7% vs 14.0%), and malocclusion (52.0% vs 26.0%) than low-traffic residents, with high noise exposure the strongest independent predictor of TMD (aOR 3.10). Exploratory mediation suggested bruxism and perceived stress accounted for 41.4% of the association, though the cross-sectional design precludes temporal inference.

papers.title: Digital dementia in adults: an assessment of digital generations.
papers.journal: Central European journal of public health
papers.summary: A cross-sectional survey in western Türkiye assessed digital dementia (DD) in adults using the Digital Dementia Scale Adult Form and Smartphone Addiction Scale, finding higher DD scores among digital natives (mean 40.56) than digital immigrants (25.17). Independent predictors of higher DD included digital native status, unmarried status, prolonged sleep onset latency, smartphone use for simple tasks, phone-related health problems, pre-sleep smartphone use, and smartphone addiction (adjusted R² = 0.681).

papers.title: Lifestyle factors or protective behaviors: which are more strongly associated with upper respiratory tract infections after COVID-19? A cross-sectional study of 1,535 Chinese college students.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional survey of 1,535 Chinese college students compared lifestyle factors and protective behaviors as correlates of upper respiratory tract infection (URTI) episodes in the post-COVID-19 period, using hierarchical negative binomial regression. Lifestyle factors contributed more to model fit than protective behaviors; daytime sleepiness, sedentary behavior, and vigorous physical activity were associated with more URTI episodes, while ≥7 h sleep, moderate physical activity, and natural ventilation were associated with fewer episodes.

papers.title: Epidemiological study of dry eye disease in Gansu Province based on mathematical modeling: analysis of regional population characteristics and identification of risk factors.
papers.summary: A cross-sectional epidemiological study of 2,000 adults in Gansu Province used logistic regression and random forest modeling to identify risk factors for dry eye disease (DED), with climate type, daily screen time, and sleep quality emerging as key predictors. The random forest model achieved an AUC of 0.832, and findings highlight regional environment, population characteristics, and lifestyle behaviors as influential.

papers.title: Integrated analysis uncovers the role of circadian rhythm genes in cold adaptation of Kandelia obovata using the multi-omics data.
papers.summary: The study assembled a chromosome-level genome of Kandelia candel and integrated comparative genomics, population resequencing, transcriptomics, and metabolomics to identify circadian rhythm-related transcription factors associated with cold adaptation in the mangrove Kandelia obovata. It prioritized 18 candidate circadian TFs, including PIF3, CCA1, LHY, and MYB members such as PAP1, and highlighted flavonoid and phenylpropanoid metabolism as downstream pathways potentially contributing to cold tolerance.

papers.title: Does Statistical Significance Imply Clinical Trustworthiness? Methodological Reflections on a Meta-Analysis of Transcutaneous Electrical Acupoint Stimulation for Managing Postoperative Sleep Quality.
papers.journal: Journal of the College of Physicians and Surgeons--Pakistan : JCPSP
papers.summary: This letter presents methodological reflections on a meta-analysis of transcutaneous electrical acupoint stimulation for postoperative sleep quality, questioning whether statistical significance alone implies clinical trustworthiness. It highlights the need to interpret meta-analytic results with attention to clinical relevance and trustworthiness.

papers.title: Case Report: Rapid resolution of psychogenic cough in an adolescent following bromazepam treatment.
papers.summary: This case report describes a 13-year-old male with severe somatic cough syndrome (psychogenic cough) that resolved completely within 24-36 hours after short-term bromazepam treatment. At 3-month follow-up, the patient remained symptom-free without medication, suggesting benzodiazepines may be an alternative when behavioral therapy is unavailable.

topic.label: Sleep Homeostasis
topic.description: Sleep pressure, recovery, circadian interactions, and longitudinal regulation of NREM/REM sleep.
